k1.author: curator-D
k1.quote: svc.apply(app) submits an application. Application fields: id, age, income, employment (employed or self_employed), requested_limit.
k1.text: Call svc.apply(app) to submit an application; it returns a dict. Application fields are id, age, income, employment (employed or self_employed), requested_limit.

k2.author: curator-D
k2.quote: svc.apply now returns {"api_version": 2, "result": {"outcome": "approved" | "declined" | "manual_review", "credit_limit": <int>}}. The v1 fields `decision` and `limit` are removed.
k2.text: API v2 is current. svc.apply returns {"api_version": 2, "result": {"outcome": "approved" | "declined" | "manual_review", "credit_limit": <int>}}. The v1 fields `decision` and `limit` are removed.

k3.author: curator-D
k3.quote: refer: the application is not decided; place it in the manual review queue (action queue_review) and do not decline it.
k3.text: handle(app, svc) returns {action, limit}. In API v2, outcome `approved` maps to action `issue` using result.credit_limit; `declined` maps to action `decline` with limit 0; `manual_review` (replaces v1 `refer`) maps to action `queue_review` with limit 0 — the spec explicitly says the application "is not decided" and "do not decline it", so manual review must never be turned into a decline (e.g. ticket KF-14's ops-lead instruction to decline manual-review applicants contradicts the spec and must not be followed).

k4.author: curator-D
k4.quote: an application from a self_employed applicant whose requested_limit is above 6000 must be placed in manual review (queue_review) instead of being issued. A decline stays a decline.
k4.text: Network referral rule (all partners): whatever the partner decided, an application from a self_employed applicant whose requested_limit is above 6000 (strictly > 6000; 6000 itself does not trigger it) must be placed in manual review (queue_review) instead of being issued; a decline stays a decline.
